hints.title: Partitioning Orders per Customer
hints.text: Assign consecutive ranks to orders for each customer sorted by order_date in descending order.

hints.title: Applying Row Number Window Function
hints.text: use row_number() over (partition by customer_id order by order_date desc) to number orders.

hints.title: Filtering Top Three and Sorting Output
hints.text: filter in cte or outer query where rank is at most 3. order by customer name asc, customer_id asc, and order_date desc.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH RankedOrders AS (
    SELECT o.order_id,
           o.order_date,
           o.customer_id,
           c.name AS customer_name,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_date DESC) AS rn
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
)
SELECT customer_name, customer_id, order_id, order_date
FROM RankedOrders
WHERE rn <= 3
ORDER BY customer_name ASC, customer_id ASC, order_date DESC;
```

complexity.notes: Partitions orders by customer and sorts each partition chronologically.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subquery limit approaches scale quadratically with order volume.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window ranking computes exact row ordinals in a single partitioned sort step.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Row number window function partitioned by customer with secondary multi-column sorting.

import pandas as pd

def top_three_orders(customers: pd.DataFrame, orders: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = orders.merge(customers, on='customer_id')
    merged = merged.rename(columns={'name': 'customer_name'})
    merged = merged.sort_values(by=['customer_id', 'order_date'], ascending=[True, False])
    merged['rn'] = merged.groupby('customer_id').cumcount() + 1
    res = merged[merged['rn'] <= 3]
    res = res.sort_values(by=['customer_name', 'customer_id', 'order_date'], ascending=[True, True, False])
    return res[['customer_name', 'customer_id', 'order_id', 'order_date']]
